review_notes: I read all 1008 lines of Mathlib/Topology/VectorBundle/Basic.lean and checked every simp/mfld_simps registration against the definitions it mentions, against the simps-generated lemmas for `Pretrivialization.linearEquivAt`, `Trivialization.continuousLinearMapAt`, `Trivialization.continuousLinearEquivAt`, `VectorBundle.continuousLinearEquivAt`, `VectorBundleCore.toFiberBundleCore`, and against downstream files: Mathlib/Topology/VectorBundle/Hom.lean, Riemannian.lean, Constructions.lean, Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/VectorBundle/Hom.lean, Mathlib/Topology/FiberBundle/Trivialization.lean, Mathlib/Topology/FiberBundle/Basic.lean and Mathlib/Data/Bundle.lean. I grepped for reverse-direction rewrites such as `← Trivialization.symmL_apply` or `← ... coe_linearMapAt_of_mem`, found none, and do not claim any rewrite cycle. Most of the interface is deliberate and consistent: `localTriv_continuousLinearMapAt` and the simps lemma for `continuousLinearMapAt` both reduce to `Z.coordChange _ _ b v`, and `localTrivAt_def`/`baseSet_at` terminate. Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean, so the shape of the `@[simps]` lemmas is inferred from declared projection options and existing `simp only` call sites; I cannot confirm experimentally whether the final definitional-equality check hides the overlap in finding 2 for closed goals. Also noted but not reported as simp defects: `Pretrivialization.linearMapAt_eq_zero` duplicates `Pretrivialization.linearMapAt_def_of_notMem`; `localTrivAt_apply_mk` is subsumed by `localTrivAt_apply`; `localTriv_symm_fst` restates `FiberBundleCore.localTriv_symm_apply` under a different name.

findings.problem: The junk-value side of the `linearMapAt` family has no simp coverage, even though the file deliberately defines these maps to be `0` off the base set (lines 39-42). The inverse family does have such coverage: `Pretrivialization.symmₗ_apply_of_notMem` (lines 101-104), `Trivialization.symmₗ_apply_of_notMem` (lines 216-219) and `Trivialization.symmL_apply_of_notMem` (lines 432-435) are all `@[simp]`. For the forward maps only the membership case is registered (`coe_linearMapAt_of_mem` lines 131-134 and 231-234, plus the hand-written `continuousLinearMapAt_apply_of_mem` lines 409-412). The complementary statements here, at 149-151 and at 245-247 carry no attribute and have no pointwise or continuous counterpart. So with `hb : b ∉ e.baseSet` in context, neither `e.linearMapAt R b y` nor `e.continuousLinearMapAt R b y` reduces to `0` by `simp`. Users must name the non-simp lemma or unfold via the equally non-simp `coe_linearMapAt`. The interface is one-sided for a family whose zero junk is part of its documented contract. The statement is also duplicated under two names, `linearMapAt_def_of_notMem` and `linearMapAt_eq_zero`, so registering one leaves a duplicate.
findings.proposed_change: Register the notMem forms in both namespaces: mark `Pretrivialization.linearMapAt_def_of_notMem` and `Trivialization.linearMapAt_def_of_notMem` as `@[simp]`, after deleting the duplicate `Pretrivialization.linearMapAt_eq_zero`, so that under `hb : b ∉ e.baseSet` the canonical rewrite is `e.linearMapAt R b = 0`. The continuous version then follows automatically, because `continuousLinearMapAt` and `linearMapAt` are tied together by the simps lemma and `LinearMap.zero_apply` is already simp. Optionally add the pointwise companion `linearMapAt_apply_of_notMem : e.linearMapAt R b y = 0`, mirroring `symmₗ_apply_of_notMem` and `continuousLinearMapAt_apply_of_mem`.
findings.benefit: Goals about the total maps outside their base set become solvable by `simp` alone, and the forward and inverse halves of the `linearMapAt`/`symmₗ` API get matching simp behaviour, so users no longer need to know the by-name lemma. The hypothesis `b ∉ e.baseSet` is the complement of the one in `coe_linearMapAt_of_mem`, so the two rules cannot fire together and no loop is introduced (this is not verified by execution).

findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
theorem continuousLinearEquivAt_apply' (e : Trivialization F (π F E)) [e.IsLinear R]
    (x : TotalSpace F E) (hx : x ∈ e.source) :
    e.continuousLinearEquivAt R x.proj (e.mem_source.1 hx) x.2 = (e x).2 := rfl
findings.problem: Two simp rules overlap on the same expression. `continuousLinearEquivAt` is declared `@[simps -fullyApplied apply symm_apply]` at line 448, so the coercion of `e.continuousLinearEquivAt R b hb` is already a simp rewrite whose value at a point is `(e ⟨b, v⟩).2`. Instantiating that rule with `b := x.proj` and `v := x.2` (the proof argument coming from proof irrelevance) matches exactly the `@[simp]` left-hand side above. The two rules give syntactically different right-hand sides, `(e ⟨x.proj, x.2⟩).2` and `(e x).2`, which agree only by structure eta. `Bundle.TotalSpace.eta` is not a simp lemma, so the simplifier has no rewrite connecting them. Which normal form a `simp` call produces is therefore decided by rule selection rather than by a declared canonical form, and only the reflexive case is rescued by the final definitional-equality check. Once the term sits inside a larger context that must match the `(e x).2` shape, `simp` can fail although the forms are `rfl`-equal. The lemma has no consumers in the library: a search finds only its declaration. Downstream files rely on the generated `Trivialization.continuousLinearEquivAt_apply` instead.
findings.proposed_change: Keep a single registration. Either drop `@[simp]` from `continuousLinearEquivAt_apply'` and leave it as a convenience lemma, or restate its right-hand side as `(e ⟨x.proj, x.2⟩).2` to match the normal form produced by the `simps` `apply` rule of `continuousLinearEquivAt` (line 448). A third option is to state it in the generated style, with an explicit hypothesis `hb : x.proj ∈ e.baseSet` and argument `x.2`, so that it is literally an instance of the existing rule.
findings.benefit: A single, unambiguous normal form for applied `continuousLinearEquivAt` terms removes dependence on simp-rule ordering and makes `simp`/`simp only` results for trivialization coordinates predictable, instead of sometimes yielding `(e x).2` and sometimes `(e ⟨x.proj, x.2⟩).2`.

evidence.excerpt: theorem TotalSpace.eta (z : TotalSpace F E) : TotalSpace.mk z.proj z.2 = z := rfl
